overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting an insufficiently specific May 25 notice; minutes and other allegations were not violations or were declined. No further remedial action because the project was withdrawn.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 25 notice topic 'Bailey Project Special Permit' failed to disclose the intended occupant (Carvana) of the site.
allegations.key_passage: Although including the name of the intended occupant of the site on the meeting notice may have been useful to the public, we find that it was not required as neither the Chair nor the Town Planner were aware of this detail at the time the meeting notice was posted.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 25 notice topic 'Bailey Project Special Permit' did not disclose that the proposed use was a used vehicle processing facility.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the meeting notice did not sufficiently advise members of the public that the Board would be discussing a large used vehicle processing facility.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged insufficient notices for Board meetings held more than 30 days before the June 24 complaint filing.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any allegations regarding insufficient meeting notices of Board meetings that took place more than 30 days prior to the date the complaints were filed, June 24, as they could have been discovered at the time the meetings took place.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged minutes approved more than 30 days before the June 24 filing were deficient.
allegations.key_passage: Similarly, we decline to review any meeting minutes which were approved more than 30 days prior to June 24.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 12 minutes were insufficiently detailed because they used a different project name than the intended occupant.
allegations.key_passage: We find these minutes to be detailed and accurate as the Town Planner merely informed the Board that he had received approximately 300 pages of plans

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 25 minutes were insufficiently detailed because they did not use the occupant's name for the project.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the minutes of the May 25 meeting are accurate and sufficiently detailed, and therefore we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law with regard to the accuracy of the meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant raised additional allegations in the request for further review, which the AG declined to address.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any additional allegations made in the request for further review.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
